item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Russia struck a Ukrainian railway station with a drone, killing 13 people. In the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky, a localized cease-fire entered its third day while attacks on aid vehicles continue. The independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta announced it will shut down after pressure from the Kremlin. The US approved a sale of 500 Patriot missiles worth $2.1 billion to Ukraine, and the conflict caused 75,767 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Israel, Gaza and the West Bank: the situation
item.description:
Israeli forces are demolishing homes of Palestinians accused of a Hebron shooting while also razing homes of gunmen linked to that attack, intensifying displacement in the West Bank. The IDF struck Gaza, killing a Hamas commander who had held hostages and wounding 14 people in a southern Gaza drone strike. Shin Bet is now permitting Hamas operatives to choose whether they are killed alone or with their families, and settlers attacked West Bank olive harvesters, wounding three. The UN rights office warned of an ethnic-cleansing nightmare in Gaza and a UN commission reported war crimes and genocide after a ceasefire, and 21,440 battle-related deaths occurred in 2024, according to UCDP.

Iran's IRGC navy says four tankers struck mines and three to four tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, while Oman rescued 25 people from a burning tanker there. Qatar's negotiators have returned to Tehran for a last-ditch mediation effort and Pakistan's army says it is cautiously optimistic about US-Iran mediation. JD Vance sent a letter to Iran's president urging a restart of peace talks, and the United States cancelled the G20 family photo after European ministers refused to stand with Russia's Lavrov. 123 battle-related deaths occurred in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:
Jordan launched air strikes in Syria in response to a church shooting, while Syrian and Jordanian officials gave conflicting accounts of the civilian casualties. Flash floods across Syria killed five children among seven victims and injured several others. A Syrian hacker received a 42‑month prison sentence for attacks on Western media and the U.S. government. Iraqi prime minister visited Syria amid security challenges in the north and south, and landmine explosions killed two children and wounded three more. The UCDP recorded 2,732 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:

Iranian-linked attacks continue, including an Iranian strike that prompted a Navy corpsman and Marine Raiders to rescue French soldiers from a burning building, and a memorial was unveiled in Erbil for victims of the 2024 Iranian missile attack. The Sudanese army is accused of carrying out 162 drone attacks from Ethiopian territory, a claim Ethiopia denies. A Rapid Support Forces commander has defected from Hemedti’s forces, and an investigation has identified commanders linked to wartime rape. The UAE federal court sentenced eight people to life imprisonment for illegal arms supplies to Sudan’s army. There were 4,680 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:

Communal violence has forced 15,000 civilians to flee Gbudwe and 27,000 displaced in Upper Nile as rival groups battle in Lakes state, prompting the detention of 16 community leaders and the launch of peace talks in Tonj East. IGAD is probing the Bentiu attacks, and a drone strike on a market in the disputed Abyei region killed 73 people, according to Addis Standard. The UCDP recorded 2 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

Gunfire is being heard near the Ethiopian-Kenya border as civilians continue to evacuate, and Ethiopia and Eritrea have severed diplomatic ties, raising regional tension. Russian Su-35 fighter jets and S-400 air defence systems have been deployed in Ethiopia as fighting spreads across Tigray, Amhara and Oromia. item.title: Somalia: the situation
item.description:
Al-Shabaab intensified assaults on Somali army positions in Lower Shabelle, killing a former al-Shabaab finance chief and raising the army toll, while Somali forces reported recapturing about 55% of territory previously held by al-Shabaab and ISIS. African Union peacekeepers are withdrawing from four bases in Lower Shabelle and Ethiopia is pulling more than 3,000 troops from Somalia, further reducing external military presence. Somalia agreed to acquire Pakistani JF‑17 fighter jets and the UAE carried out its first drone strike against al-Shabaab in nearly a year. Piracy off Somalia’s coast is rising, with hijacked oil tankers and hostages reported. The conflict caused 2,284 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
